criteria.bounded_grants: Start from the checkpoint rule and add portable proof: reads mint expiring grants over targets, versions, outcomes and checkpoints, commits validate them against the fence plus a revocation list, and spends accept only dispatch-fresh grants. Because no current draft target distinguishes granted from fenced reads (no workflow needs named expirable evidence), all present behavior matches the checkpoint rule while the grant machinery prices itself immediately — lifecycle, retention, expiry basis, diagnostics, projection support, per-commit revocation consults — with debuggability paying from day one as every authorization carries invisible-or-annotated grant state. The highest cost of the four for auditability shaped evidence no customer requested.
criteria.checkpoint_fence: Extend what the storage layer already proves: enroll each operation's reads at one checkpoint in the settled database-wide fence and revalidate permission plus revocation at commit, failing closed. No new read kind, no annotation, no rewrite — 473 pure-position lines and 288 spend effects keep their shape, transitive effects open ordinary fresh checkpoints, and the only new specified behavior is the commit-time revalidation pass with invalidating-read attribution. Price: that pass doubles predicate work per mutation; conflict rates track dependency contention; revocation bookkeeping couples globally through the shared revision until narrowed fencing is proven; D1 contention, already the top runtime uncertainty, absorbs the most load under this rule.
criteria.pinned_snapshots: Pay for precision where it narrows cost: pin observed versions per read, assert pins plus live authority at commit, and shrink the void surface from the whole database to pinned records plus authority tables — contention drops exactly where unrelated writes are common. Eventual views take a declared label or they do not exist; unlabeled reads stay pinned-safe. Price: pin capture/assertion machinery, a second read kind with diagnostics and teaching, D1 narrowed-assertion proof (or collapse into the checkpoint rule with stranded bookkeeping), and recurring authorizing-versus-eventual adjudication — a moderate permanent tax for contention relief that only matters if the database-wide assertion actually bites.
criteria.read_at_effect: Trade surface for reads: no checkpoints, no pins, no grants — each effect reads live state at claim time and the snapshot contract vanishes with its specification, diagnostics and teaching cost. Multi-effect operations pay per-effect authorization reads instead, let bindings need their live-or-captured ruling once, and write-write conflicts keep the existing fence with no addition. Price: the migration bill lands on authors — every read-guard-act site is either silently redefined or rewritten with re-queries and T36-style proof — while read amplification taxes every hot multi-effect path permanently and informal let-smuggling recreates the gap the rule deleted, leaving fence complexity plus N reads plus folk workarounds.

read_rule.instructions: For the authoritative-read gate, which rule best preserves the six accepted workflows, keeps stale reads and mid-flight revocation from silently authorizing commits and spends, and minimizes semantic surface, migration churn and contention risk? Judge every option under the same workflow-preservation and minimal-intervention constraints.

state: Cost and churn frame this gate: 473 pure-position lines in 50 files plus 288 spend effects (236 sends, 69 targets, 22 money-creates, 27 allowance-sets) price each option differently, from zero edits to per-site rewrites with proof burden, and from no new surface to grants with revocation infrastructure. The settled substrate costs nothing further: D1 database-wide optimistic fencing, admission evaluation with commit-time permission recheck, atomic dispatch guard-plus-claim, mandate-checked payment collect, reread-marked display reads. Six workflow bar items (Chat spend, can_use, Creative guard, Check heartbeat and their fencing) set the preservation standard regardless of price, and live revocation immediacy (Grant deactivate-then-deny) must survive under any winner. Priced uncertainties: T06 narrowing and T16/T17a-plus-verified-T17b landed with T28-A same-owner fencing and T31a flat staging, while T29 atomicity is owed; evidence shows zero intra-operation gap executions (9 candidates, 31 conflict rows, no active_member or let observations) with the R29 flip open and T23/T22/T21 pending; fence proof stays plan-not-proof under memory limits with DECISIONS #138 open; active_member remains barred from pure positions without a bounded-read contract; T24 has no dispatch record; D1 contention leads runtime uncertainty. This is a design choice, not a measured implementation result.
